newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY UNION-AUSTRALIA AND NEW ZEALAND COACHES IN PRE-TEST SPAT.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-AUSTRALIA AND NEW ZEALAND COACHES IN PRE-TEST SPAT.

text.p: A public slanging match broke out on Friday between the Australian and New Zealand rugby union coaches ahead of Saturday's test.

Australia coach Greg Smith repeated his claim that the All Blacks had used blatant fouls during their 30-13 win in the first match of the three-match Bledisloe Cup series between the two traditional rivals in Christchurch a fortnight ago.
New Zealand's John Hart hit back, saying that Smith's reported comments that the Wallabies would "take matters into their own hands" was against the spirit of the game.
"I don't doubt for one second that the All Blacks had won the (first) match but I think it was probably about a 10-point game in the end," Smith told a news conference on Friday.
"We weren't able to get the points because of the continual infringements and I don't think it's good for our game.
"I think the players got sick of what was going on. I think it had become farcical at the end," he said.

Smith was highly critical of the performance by referee Ed Morrison in the first match but said he was satisfied with the outcome of a meeting with Morrison soon after the Englishman arrived on Thursday.
Hart was already in a bad mood because his team had only a week to prepare after their epic 35-32 win over South Africa in the opening match of the tri-nations series in Johannesburg.
Smith's reported comments darkened Hart's mood further ahead of a match expected to be played in front of an Australian record crowd of about 100,000 at the Melbourne Cricket Ground.
"He's told his team that if there were any illegal tactics or professional fouls he would expect the players to take the matter into their own hands," Hart told reporters.
"And if that meant that an all-in brawl was necessary from the Wallabies, then he would accept that, and if that meant an Australian was to be sent off, then he would accept that.
"I'm really disappointed with a comment from an international coach that even indicates that. I don't believe that sort of attitude has any...place in the game of rugby."
The only injury concern in either camp is over New Zealand captain and hooker Sean Fitzpatrick, whose knee injury will be assessed on Saturday.
Hart rated Fitzpatrick a "50-50 chance", but said Auckland's Norm Hewitt would take over as hooker if Fitzpatrick was ruled out. Number eight Zinzan Brooke would then assume the captaincy.
